title: The Ando Handle
text: Read the Building, an homage to the 2021 exhibition on rules. A building is a stack of rules, and some are hiding in plain sight. Start at the door: a stock lever, used so often by Ando that its maker named it after him.

title: Six Holes a Panel
text: Concrete remembers its moulds. Each plywood panel is 900 by 1800 mm, and the ties that held it leave six holes on a 450 by 600 mm grid. The blue outline shows two panels; count the rest yourself.

title: Tread 300, Rise 150
text: The stair follows the same grid: 300 mm treads to match the tie holes, 150 mm rises, a sixth of a panel. Our model misses this by about 2 cm a step, and we would rather tell you than hide it.

title: Solid Steel
text: The court glass is held by solid steel mullions, only 235 by 69 mm, because hollow ones would have to be fatter. The tallest reach about 11.7 m.

title: Should Every Rule Be Written?
text: A question for you. Step on a square to vote. The tally lives only on this device, which is a rule too.

title: Square Goes
text: Forty-two squares and one rule. Keep left and lanes appear; follow the one ahead and a queue forms; take the rule away and they bump. Tap a square to change the rule.

title: 16 mm, 54 m, 30 mm
text: The roof: 16 mm steel plate, welded on site because 54 m could not travel by road, and built to move by up to 30 mm with the heat. Rules of transport and weather, folded into one shape.
